appraisal_events.evidence: « qu'à sa propre belle-soeur, et qui avait une si haute idée de lui, il niât me connaître, fait si naturel puisque je connaissais à la fois sa tante et son neveu »
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus denies knowing the narrator to his own sister-in-law despite an obvious, natural acquaintance, an unexplained social disavowal that excludes the narrator.

appraisal_events.evidence: « il ne tendit pas la main à Bloch... il lui répondit de l'air le plus insolent, d'une voix irritée et blessante »
appraisal_events.explanation: After apparently seeming friendly to Bloch beforehand, Charlus publicly refuses to shake his hand and answers him with open hostility, humiliating him in front of others.

status_effects.explanation: Charlus's unexplained denial of acquaintance to his sister-in-law is a mild social exclusion of the narrator, though the narrator registers it more as puzzlement than as injury.
Bloch is publicly and pointedly humiliated by Charlus's refusal to shake hands and hostile tone, leaving him 'éreinté' and estranged from the narrator for six months.

ambiguities: Charlus's contradictory behavior toward the narrator (blushing at him, then denying knowing him) and toward Bloch (seeming friendly in the street, then snubbing him publicly) is explicitly flagged by the narrator as a mystery whose explanation is deferred to later (Sodome I); this passage withholds judgment on Charlus's own character rather than resolving it, so no status effect was scored for Charlus himself.

The passage's 'Mme de Stermaria' does not clearly match the candidate 'M. de Stermaria' in the alias map, and in any case the narrator's anticipation of the dinner with her is framed as a general reflection on desire and time rather than a staged evaluative event, so no event was scored for that figure.
